## Results

- LASSO feature selection across 369 physiological, behavioral and dietary measures on 238 cadets, over academic, physical and military outcomes
- Inference runs on held-out data through sample splitting, cross-validated R2 and a permutation null, so selection and testing never happen on the same rows
- On synthetic data with a planted signal the pipeline recovers exactly the planted predictors and returns a null model for a pure-noise outcome

## The problem

West Point assesses cadets on three pillars: academic, physical, and military. With hundreds of measurements from wearables, surveys, blood work, and diet records, which of them actually carry information about each pillar, and do the pillars share predictors?

## What I built

I joined device-based sleep and activity data with demographic, fitness, psychosocial, dietary and biomarker measures for a Fall 2024 cohort, with data collection supported by USARIEM. I used 10-fold cross-validated LASSO to select predictors for each outcome, then ran the inference on held-out data so that selection and testing never touch the same rows. The public repository runs end to end on a synthetic dataset with a planted signal, so anyone can check the pipeline without study records.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
## What it is for

Where to invest in cadet support: if academic and physical performance respond to measurable, changeable factors while military performance does not, resources for the military pillar belong in mentorship and experience rather than monitoring.
:::

## Tools

R, glmnet, tidyverse

[The public repository ships code and synthetic data. The study data is human-subjects research and stays private.]{.fine}
